# Step 0: Check for packages and install them if not already installed

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
# List all packages needed for this notebook
required_packages <- c("httr", "jsonlite", "dplyr")

# Check if each one is installed, and install it if missing
for (pkg in required_packages) {
  if (!require(pkg, character.only = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
    library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}

# Confirm
cat("✅ All packages loaded successfully!\n")
```

# Step 1: Setup

This notebook pulls Census data using the API and prepares it for later steps.  


```{r load packages and set up test}
# Load required packages
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)


# Simple test request to Census API
url <- "https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/pl?get=P1_001N,NAME&for=state:*"
res <- GET(url)
census_raw <- fromJSON(content(res, "text"))

# Check first 5 rows
head(census_raw)
```

``` {R combine variables and generate URLs}
# Collapse to comma-separated strings for the API 'get=' parameter
census_variables1_str <- paste(census_variables1, collapse = ",")
census_variables2_str <- paste(census_variables2, collapse = ",")
decennial_variables3_str <- paste(decennial_variables3, collapse = ",")

# Geography clause (URL-encoded spaces). State:15 = Hawaii
# Change "state:15" to a different state FIPS if needed
in_geography <- "&for=block%20group:*&in=state:15%20county:*%20tract:*"

# Combined endpoints
census_combined_url <- paste0(census_base_url, census_dataset_url)
decennial_combined_url <- paste0(census_base_url, decennial_dataset_url)

# Full query URLs (ready to GET)
cbg_url1 <- paste0(census_combined_url, "?get=", census_variables1_str, in_geography)
cbg_url2 <- paste0(census_combined_url, "?get=", census_variables2_str, in_geography)
cbg_url3 <- paste0(decennial_combined_url, "?get=", decennial_variables3_str, in_geography)

# Variable metadata (variables.json) URLs
census_fields_url1 <- paste0(census_combined_url, "/variables.json")
census_fields_url2 <- paste0(census_combined_url, "/subject/variables.json")
census_fields_url3 <- paste0(decennial_combined_url, "/variables.json")

# Quick preview (print the start of each URL to verify)

#cat("CBG URL 3 (start):\n", substr(cbg_url3, 1, 200), "...\n\n")


```

# Step 4 Define function to fetch data from Census API and store in lists

```{R Define fetch function}
# Define a small helper function to fetch and convert JSON to data.frame
fetch_census <- function(url) {
  resp <- httr::GET(url)
  if (resp$status_code != 200) {
    stop(paste("Request failed with status", resp$status_code))
  }
  
  # Convert JSON text to list, then to data.frame
  raw_json <- httr::content(resp, "text")
  data_list <- jsonlite::fromJSON(raw_json)
  
  # The first row of Census API results contains the column names
  df <- as.data.frame(data_list[-1, ], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(df) <- data_list[1, ]
  
  return(df)
}
```

```{R Run function to pull data from Census API}
# Fetch each dataset
cbg1 <- fetch_census(cbg_url1)
cbg2 <- fetch_census(cbg_url2)
cbg3 <- fetch_census(cbg_url3)

# Print quick summaries to verify
cat("✅ Downloads complete!\n")
cat("Rows in cbg1:", nrow(cbg1), "\n")
cat("Rows in cbg2:", nrow(cbg2), "\n")
cat("Rows in cbg3:", nrow(cbg3), "\n\n")

# Peek at the structure of one
head(cbg1[, 1:6])
```


# Merge first two block group dataframes

```{r Merge Second DF with First, echo=TRUE}
# Drop duplicate columns (except GEO_ID) from cbg2
duplicate_columns <- intersect(names(cbg2), names(cbg1))
duplicate_columns <- setdiff(duplicate_columns, "GEO_ID")

if (length(duplicate_columns) > 0) {
  message("Dropping duplicate columns: ", paste(duplicate_columns, collapse = ", "))
  cbg2 <- cbg2[ , !(names(cbg2) %in% duplicate_columns)]
}

# Merge cbg1 and cbg2 on GEO_ID
cbg <- merge(cbg1, cbg2, by = "GEO_ID", all.x = TRUE, suffixes = c("", "_2"))

# Quick check
cat("Merged dataframe has", nrow(cbg), "rows and", ncol(cbg), "columns\n")
head(cbg)
```
``` {R Merge Third DF with previously merged}
# Drop duplicate columns (except GEO_ID) from cbg3
duplicate_columns <- intersect(names(cbg3), names(cbg))
duplicate_columns <- setdiff(duplicate_columns, "GEO_ID")

if (length(duplicate_columns) > 0) {
  message("Dropping duplicate columns: ", paste(duplicate_columns, collapse = ", "))
  cbg3 <- cbg3[ , !(names(cbg3) %in% duplicate_columns)]
}

# Merge cbg (from previous step) with cbg3
cbg <- merge(cbg, cbg3, by = "GEO_ID", all.x = TRUE, suffixes = c("", "_3"))

# Quick check
cat("Merged dataframe now has", nrow(cbg), "rows and", ncol(cbg), "columns\n")
head(cbg)
```

``` {R replace nulls with zeroes}
cbg[is.na(cbg)] <- 0

# Check if there are any nulls left
print(any(is.na(cbg)))

```

``` {R convert numbers in DF to actual numeric fields}
# Loop over all columns
for (colname in names(cbg)) {
  # Try converting to numeric
  numeric_col <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cbg[[colname]]))
  
  # If there are no new NAs introduced, replace the column
  if (!all(is.na(numeric_col) & !is.na(cbg[[colname]]))) {
    cbg[[colname]] <- numeric_col
  }
}

# Quick check: see the classes of all columns
sapply(cbg, class)
```


``` {R create and calculate new LimitedEnglishHH field for limited english speaking households}

# Check input fields first
print(sapply(cbg[, c("C16002_004E", "C16002_007E", "C16002_010E", "C16002_013E")], class))
print(head(cbg[, c("C16002_004E", "C16002_007E", "C16002_010E", "C16002_013E")], 10))

# Create a new column by summing other columns
cbg$LimitedEnglishHH <- cbg$C16002_004E + 
                        cbg$C16002_007E + 
                        cbg$C16002_010E + 
                        cbg$C16002_013E

# Preview the first few rows
head(cbg$LimitedEnglishHH)
```
